_readme: Every number in here is a tuning knob. Change a value, reload the page, done - no code changes.
Temperatures are in degrees Celsius. Ambient (air) temperature starts at 8 and is set by the slider.
group         which heading the button appears under in the side panel
category      static = never moves | powder = falls and piles | liquid = falls and spreads | gas = rises
density       heavier sinks through lighter. This is what makes sand sink, ice float and oil sit on water.
fallSpeed     max cells moved per frame (rise speed for gases)
fallChance    fraction of frames gravity acts; used when even one cell per frame is too fast
slide         powders only: chance of sliding diagonally. 0.9 = loose (dry sand), 0.1 = sluggish (wet mud)
repose        powders only: how far the ground beside it has to fall away before it will slip.
1 = collapses into a flat cone (dry sand), 5 = holds a steep heap (wet mud).
This is the angle of repose, and it is what makes wet ground look different from dry.
spread        liquids only: how far sideways it will look for somewhere to fall from
flowSteps     liquids only: how many sideways moves it gets per frame. This is the main dial for how
quickly a poured puddle settles down flat. Water 4, oil 3, lava 1 (it barely creeps).
moveChance    chance it shifts about of its own accord this frame - creeping, sliding, settling.
Lower = thick and sticky (lava, wet mud). Falling is not covered by it: gravity is
not a matter of choice, so everything drops at its own fallSpeed whatever this says.
displacesMaterials  false makes gravity stop at occupied cells instead of density-swapping through them.
drift         gases only: chance of wandering sideways
conductivity  how fast this material takes on its neighbours' temperature (0 = perfect insulator)

thermalNetworkRate  direct heat-transfer fraction per local fast-network substep; 0 disables it. The fast network links listed conductors with one another and enclosed air/gas only; ordinary conductivity still handles other contact pairs.
ambientCooling  set false to let a material retain its stored temperature instead of drifting toward adjacent air
cooling       how fast it drifts back to the air temperature on its own, as a fraction of the gap
coolingVariance  +/- fraction applied to each particle's cooling speed, using its fixed variation
conductive    whether Sparks can send a power pulse through this material
electricalConductivity  relative pulse speed through a conductor; higher values move pulses faster
machine       specialized machine behavior, such as the directional Fan, Heater or Cooler
machineTemp   target temperature emitted by a powered directional machine
machineRange  number of cells reached by a powered directional machine
machineRate   fraction of the target temperature applied each frame
machineEmits  material id/name launched from the front of a powered machine
projectile    moves a transient ray in the direction stored in its cell data
projectileSpeed  cells advanced per frame by a directional projectile
alpha         normal-view opacity, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid)
chargeCapacity  stored electrical charge; 0 means it cannot retain charge between pulses
chargePerSpark  total charge one Spark adds, shared by the connected storage-metal mass
chargeSparkChance  chance per frame at full charge of emitting a visual-only Spark
dischargeBattery  draws stored charge from touching battery material and conducts its power
powerConsumption  charge units this conductive cell draws from its connected Battery grid each tick
wireReach     extra grid cells of empty air a wire can bridge to reach another conductor
bulkInsulation  how much slower buried cells exchange heat than exposed cells, from 0 to 1
coolsBy       degrees given up per frame on its own account, whatever the air is doing, stopping
at the air temperature. This is how something that starts white hot cools: at its
own pace rather than twice as fast because the weather turned, and evenly through
the whole of it, so a lava flow stiffens all at once instead of from the edges in.
defaultTemp   the temperature it is created at
emit          a heat source holds itself at this temperature (fire, lava). Water can overwhelm it.
emitRate      how strongly it holds that temperature. Lower = easier to quench.
radiates      degrees per frame thrown at all eight neighbours, on top of what conduction carries.
This is how fire spreads sideways: a flame rises off whatever lit it far too fast to
warm its neighbours by touch, so without this a pool of oil would sit under a fire
and never light, and a row of plants would only ever burn from below. Nothing is
heated past the temperature of whatever is heating it.
clings        chance per frame that a flame stays put instead of rising, while there is something
flammable beside it. Fire is a gas, so without this it leaves the moment it appears
and never stays next to anything long enough to light it.
glowTemp      temperature where glowColor is fully reached, or the fully-hot point in a color/color2 gradient.
Heat sources default to their emit temperature; cooling scoria names its own hot point.
glowStartTemp  temperature where a material starts blending from its base color toward glowColor
glowColor      optional hot color reached at glowTemp; the blend changes appearance only, not heat
forceTemp     drags its cell to this temperature in BOTH directions - used by the two ray tools,
which is how the cold ray can chill things rather than only heat them
forceRate     how hard it drags
meltPoint     above this temperature it turns into meltsInto
freezePoint   below this temperature it turns into freezesInto
freezeNeedsGround  it has to have landed on something before it will set solid. Scoria uses this,
so a sinking lump keeps sinking instead of turning to stone in mid water and
leaving a slab of it hanging with nothing underneath.
insulatedBy   what counts as being buried - list the material itself as well, since lava under
more lava is just as covered up as lava under a crust - and insulatedCooling is
how much of its own cooling is left while it is. It is the cell directly above
that decides, which is all being buried amounts to one cell at a time.
In short:
own cooling is left while one is lying on it. Buried scoria gives up heat a tenth
as fast as bare scoria, and buried lava a tenth as fast again - a hundredth of the
open rate - so a flow that has crusted over stays molten underneath for a long
time, and only what is actually exposed to the sky sets at any speed.
bedrockKeepsMolten  resting on the very bottom row of the world, it never sets by cooling alone -
the floor of the world is the heat the world sits on. Water can still put it out.
boilPoint     above this temperature it turns into boilsInto and puffs out boilEmits
evaporatesAbove  above this temperature the particle is removed instead of changing into another material
evaporationHumidity  local relative-humidity points restored before evaporation removes the particle
depositPoint  a gas condensing where the AIR is below this turns straight into depositsInto,
a solid, instead of into a liquid. This is steam falling as snow rather than rain.
condenseLossChance  chance that a particle disappears when it is due to condense, decided then
contacts      what it turns into depending on what it comes to rest ON: snow melting the
moment it lands in water, or packing down into ice where it settles on ice
convertsBelow gradually changes the material directly underneath while contact is maintained.
windLift      how readily the wind tool picks it up, 0 to 1. Leave it out and it follows from
the category: gases 1, powders 0.5, liquids 0.1, anything fixed 0.
tool          marks an entry as a tool rather than a material. The wind tool is not placed
into the world; dragging it blows things about and stirs up the air.
ignitePoint   above this temperature it catches fire: becomes burnsInto for burnLife frames, leaving emberInto
quenchedInto  what it becomes the moment it touches water (the water flashes to steam)
wetsInto      what a dry powder becomes when a filtering drop reaches it. The drop is consumed.
latent        how much heat it has to soak up past the threshold before the change actually happens.
This is why ice sits in a puddle for a few seconds instead of vanishing, but melts
almost instantly against a flame. 0 means the change is immediate.
blastRadius   how far the explosion reaches. Anything explosive lights a fuse instead of burning.
fuse          frames between being lit and going off
blastProof    survives explosions (wall, glass and ceramic do)
growHeight    the tallest a plant can grow, in cells. growHeightMin is the shortest; each plant
picks a height somewhere between the two, so a row of them is not all one size.
growChance    chance per frame of putting on another cell of growth
flowerInto    what the growing tip opens into when it is fully grown. Leave it out and the plant
simply stops - which is what grass on wet sand does.
seedChance    chance per frame that a flower drops a seed
seedWaterRange  how close water has to be before it will set seed at all - this far to the sides
and above, and four times as far below, since the flower is up on a stem while the
water it lives on is down at the roots. A plant somewhere dry lives out its life
but never reproduces.
sprouts       what a seed can come up on and what it becomes there. Wet mud gives a full plant,
wet sand gives short grass, and wet ash gives shorter yellow grass. Dry ground gives nothing.
submergedInto is what it comes up as instead when the ground it landed on is at
the bottom of open water - that is how a lily starts. The choice is made on the
single frame the seed germinates and is never looked at again, so draining the
pond afterwards leaves the lily growing.
submergedDepth  how deep the water standing over a seed has to be before it counts as being
underwater rather than in a puddle
sproutMinTemp the seed will not germinate below this temperature
growStyle     how a plant puts on growth. Left out, it climbs as an ordinary stem. "netting"
weaves up through water as an open mesh; "surface" creeps sideways along the
top of the water as a lily pad does.
floatChance   chance that a new one of these is buoyant. This is settled the moment the
particle is created and never revisited, so a seed that came up a floater stays
one. A buoyant one weighs floatDensity instead of its own density, which is what
makes it rise to the surface, ride on it and wander to one side, while the rest
of them sink straight to the bottom.
floatDensity  the weight a buoyant one has. Put it below water's density to make it float.
waterPermeability  chance each frame that water enters a wet powder; once inside it keeps filtering
downward through at most 50 powder cells. Once all reachable cells are wet, the
column is saturated and further water stays above it.
compactsInto a supported column deeper than compactDepth changes its bottom excess cells into this
compactDepth  how many loose cells remain at the top of a compacting column
soaks         this liquid filters into dry and wet powders (water does)
life          frames before it decays into decaysInto (0 = lasts forever)
decayChance   chance that a particle produces decaysInto when its life runs out
lifeTransitionAt  fraction of its lifetime at which it changes into lifeTransitionInto
lifeTransitionInto  material used for that late-life transition
sparkEmitterChance  chance per frame of emitting a Spark into an empty neighboring space; touching liquids suppress it
corrodible    whether acid can eat it
corrosion     how readily this eats through what it touches, and corrodeEmits is the gas left
behind in the hole - which is where the toxic fumes off dissolving acid come from
withersPlants what this turns any growing thing it touches into, and witherChance is how often.
Whatever does it is not used up: the fumes kill what they drift through and carry
straight on. It goes by what grows rather than by a list of names, so a new plant
added to this file is covered without anything else changing.
A note on temperatures: heat spreads by averaging with the four neighbours, so a single cell sitting
next to one flame settles at roughly a quarter of the flame temperature. That is why wood ignites at
150 rather than a realistic 300 - it is the temperature a cell can actually reach next to a fire.

1.name: Sand
1.description: Loose mineral powder that falls quickly, piles at a shallow angle, wets into Wet Sand and melts into Glass.

2.name: Water
2.description: Fast-flowing liquid that spreads and soaks powders; it freezes into Ice and boils into Steam.

3.name: Fire
3.description: Short-lived hot gas that clings to nearby fuel, radiates heat and can leave Smoke as it expires.

4.name: Ice
4.description: Light cold solid that floats on Water and melts into Water at its melt threshold.

5.name: Oil
5.description: Light slow liquid that floats on Water and ignites into Fire when heated above its ignition point.

6.name: Lava
6.description: Heavy slow molten rock that bakes ground, is quenched by Water into Scoria and cools into Stone.

7.name: Stone
7.description: Heavy insulating solid that forms a stable barrier and melts into Scoria when strongly heated.

8.name: Wet Mud
8.description: Sticky wet soil that holds steep piles, filters water and compacts into Clay when deeply supported.

9.name: Steam
9.description: Rising drifting vapor from boiling Water or Wet Mud that adds local humidity and condenses into Water or Snow when the surrounding air reaches its dewpoint.

10.name: Smoke
10.description: Lingering drifting gas from burning and condensation reactions that eventually settles into Ash; it evaporates away above 3000 C.

11.name: Wood
11.description: Fixed insulating fuel that ignites into Fire when hot and leaves Ash after burning.

12.name: Ash
12.description: Light drifting powder left by burning that melts into Lava at high heat, wets into Wet Ash and can support short grass.

13.name: Glass
13.description: Blast-proof insulating solid that melts into Lava when heated above its melt point.

14.name: Acid
14.description: Corrosive liquid that eats eligible materials, releases Toxic Gas and boils into Smoke when hot.

15.name: Plant
15.description: Growing life that climbs from wet soil, flowers at full height, burns above its ignition point and freezes into Sand.

16.name: Wall
16.description: Immovable blast-proof barrier that blocks wind and resists ordinary reactions.

17.name: Wet Sand
17.description: Damp heavy powder that holds a firmer pile, filters water and boils back into Sand with Steam.

18.name: Dry Mud
18.description: Dry soil that wets into Wet Mud when reached by water and holds a looser pile than wet ground.

19.name: Grass Seeds
19.description: Viable grass seed powder that germinates on damp soil when local temperature and humidity are suitable; dry seeds remain dormant.

20.name: Gunpowder
20.description: Explosive powder that catches above its ignition point, burns through its fuse and blasts nearby breakable material.

21.name: Spark
21.description: Short-lived drifting electrical gas that energizes touching conductors before expiring.

22.name: Heat Ray
22.description: Transient hot tool that starts upward each stroke, follows the nearest cardinal drag direction, and ramps nearby cells toward 2000 C before fading.

26.name: Snow
26.description: Very light cold powder that melts into Water, melts on Water and packs into Ice when settled on Ice.

25.name: Grass
25.description: Hardy low grass grown from Grass Seeds on damp soil; it thrives in mild temperatures and humid air and releases moisture as it grows.

24.name: Flower
24.description: Mature land flower that burns or freezes like a Plant and sets Seed only when water is nearby.

27.name: Wind
27.description: Transient tool that pushes loose materials and stirs the air without placing a material in the world.

23.name: Cold Ray
23.description: Transient cold tool that starts downward each stroke, follows the nearest cardinal drag direction, and ramps nearby cells toward -120 C before fading.

28.name: Lily Stem
28.description: Open-mesh aquatic plant grown from submerged Seeds that climbs through water and opens into Lily Pads.

29.name: Lily Pad
29.description: Surface-growing aquatic plant that spreads across water and opens into a Lily Flower.

30.name: Lily Flower
30.description: Aquatic flower that can set Seed near water and freezes or burns like other growing plants.

32.name: Toxic Gas
32.description: Lingering corrosive gas that withers growing materials and sometimes settles into Acid; it evaporates away above 3000 C.

31.name: Scoria
31.description: Cooling porous lava that sinks until supported, melts back into Lava when hot and sets into Stone when cool.

33.name: Wet Ash
33.description: Watered Ash that holds a steeper pile, supports Ash Grass and boils into Ash with Steam.

34.name: Ash Grass
34.description: Short yellow grass grown from Wet Ash that burns above its ignition point and freezes into Sand in deep cold.

35.name: Clay
35.description: Compacted wet soil that insulates moderately and fires into Ceramic above its firing temperature.

36.name: Ceramic
36.description: Blast-proof fired clay that melts into Lava only under extreme heat.

37.name: Copper
37.description: Dense conductive metal that carries power, draws from Battery and melts into Molten Copper. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

38.name: Molten Copper
38.description: Flowing conductive copper above its melt point that cools back into Copper when supported.

39.name: Battery
39.description: Conductive storage metal that shares Spark charge across connected Battery cells and melts into Molten Aluminum. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

40.name: Molten Aluminum
40.description: Flowing conductive aluminum that cools back into Battery when it reaches its freeze point and has support.

41.name: Iron
41.description: Dense conductive metal that draws battery charge for the grid and melts into Molten Iron. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

42.name: Molten Iron
42.description: Flowing conductive iron above its melt point that cools back into Iron when supported.

43.name: Spark Dust
43.description: Loose conductive powder that emits nearby Sparks until its long lifetime expires into Ash.

44.name: Spark Block
44.description: Fixed conductive spark source that emits Sparks for a long lifetime, then becomes Spark Dust near the end.

45.name: Fan
45.description: Powered one-cell machine that stores a direction and blows a widening cone of airflow through the world; its wind speed defaults to 7 on the 1-50 Breeze scale, where 50 matches the old Fan speed 15. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

46.name: Heater
46.description: Powered directional machine that heats a 28-cell cone toward 2000 C by default, with a configurable 0-4000 C target, and launches Heat Rays along its centreline while it has power. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

47.name: Cooler
47.description: Powered directional machine that chills a 28-cell cone toward -60 C by default, with a configurable -60 to 20 C target, and launches Cold Rays along its centreline while it has power. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

48.name: Powder Storage Bin
48.description: Tubing-fed storage machine that accepts one kind of powder and holds up to 500 particles.

49.name: Liquid Storage Bin
49.description: Tubing-fed storage machine that accepts one kind of liquid, including molten metal, and holds up to 500 particles.

50.name: Gas Storage Bin
50.description: Tubing-fed storage machine that accepts one kind of non-flaming gas and holds up to 500 particles.

51.name: Tubing
51.description: Dense iron tubing that carries stored material between compatible machines and rapidly transfers heat along connected metal paths or into enclosed air, but does not conduct electrical power. Its pixel color brightens toward a configured glow as it heats toward melting.

52.name: Sprinkler
52.description: Always-active machine that receives one stored material through connected Tubing and holds up to 100 particles. Release controls whether stored material is emitted; Drain Mode selects the normal downward outlet or seven-direction sprinkler spray.

53.name: Mixer
53.description: Always-active machine with two independent 500-particle Tubing inputs and a 1000-particle mixed output. It alternates the two accepted materials when releasing them below at 10 particles per second.

54.name: Insulation
54.description: Slow-cooling solid that retains heat, has zero conductivity so it blocks contact transfer, warms by radiation and melts into Lava above 5000 C.

55.name: Cloud
55.description: Visible cloud moisture forms in humid air, precipitates as rain or snow at the dewpoint, and evaporates above 100 C back into local humidity.

56.name: Corrosion
56.description: Powdery corrosion formed over time when metal touches Water or stays in saturated air; it falls away from the source metal and melts into Lava under intense heat.

57.name: Moss Spores
57.description: Fine viable spores that colonize damp wood, stone or wet ground in cool, very humid air; dry spores wait for suitable conditions.

58.name: Daffodil Seeds
58.description: Viable bulb seeds that germinate in cool, moist soil and grow into yellow Daffodils; dry seeds wait for rain.

59.name: Red Tulip Seeds
59.description: Viable tulip seeds that germinate in mild damp soil and mature into red flowers; they remain dormant while soil or air is too dry.

60.name: Geranium Seeds
60.description: Viable geranium seeds that grow in warm, moderately humid damp soil and mature into clusters of pink flowers.

61.name: Blue Flower Seeds
61.description: Viable seeds that germinate in cool, damp soil and produce blue flowers when local humidity and temperature suit the species.

62.name: Banana Seeds
62.description: Viable tropical seeds that need warm temperatures, high humidity and wet soil before they germinate into a broad-leaved Banana Plant.

63.name: Water Grass / Lily Seeds
63.description: Viable aquatic seeds that need warm, humid wet ground and open water; submerged seeds grow a mesh stem toward the surface.

64.name: Moss
64.description: Low creeping plant that spreads across damp wood, stone or wet ground in cool, very humid air and slowly releases moisture nearby.

65.name: Daffodil
65.description: Cool-season flowering plant that grows from damp soil, adds humidity and opens into a bright yellow Daffodil Bloom.

66.name: Red Tulip
66.description: Mild-climate plant that grows from damp soil, contributes humidity and matures into a vivid red Tulip Bloom.

67.name: Geranium
67.description: Warm-climate branching plant that grows on damp soil and matures into clusters of pink Geranium blooms.

68.name: Blue Flower
68.description: Cool-season plant with slender stems that grows on damp sand or ash and opens into a blue flower.

69.name: Banana Plant
69.description: Tall tropical plant that needs warm temperatures, saturated humid air and wet soil; it contributes moisture and grows a broad fruit bunch.

70.name: Water Grass
70.description: Aquatic net-forming plant that climbs through open water, spreads along its surface and contributes moisture to the local air.

71.name: Daffodil Bloom
71.description: Bright yellow flower at the mature tip of a Daffodil plant; it produces new Daffodil Seeds only while the plant is thriving.

72.name: Tulip Bloom
72.description: Red flower at the mature tip of a Red Tulip; it produces Red Tulip Seeds only while the plant is thriving.

73.name: Geranium Bloom
73.description: Pink flower cluster on a mature Geranium; it produces Geranium Seeds only while the plant is thriving.

74.name: Blue Flower Bloom
74.description: Blue flower at the mature tip of a Blue Flower plant; it produces Blue Flower Seeds only while the plant is thriving.

75.name: Banana Bunch
75.description: Mature fruiting form of a healthy Banana Plant; it produces new Banana Seeds in tropical humid conditions.

76.name: Water Grass Bloom
76.description: Aquatic flower at the surface of mature Water Grass; it produces aquatic seeds only while the rooted plant is thriving.

77.name: Water Grass Pad
77.description: Broad floating leaf that spreads along the open water surface before Water Grass blooms.

78.name: Banana Leaf
78.description: Wide, raised leaf frond on the upright Banana Plant trunk.

79.name: Stainless Steel
79.description: Rust-resistant alloy that conducts heat and carries electrical pulses more slowly than Iron.

80.name: Splitter
80.description: Tubing machine that buffers one incoming material and divides its flow evenly between two Tubing outputs.

81.name: Collector
81.description: Directional funnel that gathers ordinary powder, liquid, or gas into a one-material buffer of up to 100 particles and sends it through compatible Tubing at up to 30 units per second, limited by line capacity.
